name: Bassline / Niche / UK 4x4
summary: Relentless four-to-the-floor kick at 138–142 with a huge clap/snare on 2 and 4, open hats on every offbeat and closed hats on the syncopated 16ths between them — swung hard in the Niche era, near-straight in the modern warehouse style. Drums stay punchy and sparse because the warped bass carries the groove; character comes from hat contour, rim ghosts, conga/tambourine layers and the signature snare rushes at phrase turnarounds.

sounds.kick: Tight 909-style kick pitched up a semitone and shortened to half a beat so it clears the sub; EQ-notched at the snare fundamental.
sounds.snare: Clap on 2 and 4 with a lower snare layered ~4 dB under it; a tight, short snare for 16th/32nd rushes; rim under the clap for snap.
sounds.hats: Loud offbeat open hat (the bounce anchor), skippy closed 16ths with aggressive accent contour; a quiet ride can shadow the open hat.
sounds.percussion: Shaker and tambourine for the Niche shuffle, congas on organ tunes, a breakbeat pitched +5 with kicks removed for ghost-snare shuffle.
sounds.cymbals: Crash on drops and 8-bar markers; ride as a metallic offbeat in the dark modern lane.

machines: Roland TR-909 — kick, clap and open hat (owned)
Roland TR-808 — clap/snare layer and cowbell (owned)
Korg M1 drums — the organ-bassline era kit (owned)
Akai MPC2000 / MPC3000 — chopping and swing for Niche-era tunes (owned)
Breakbeat libraries — pitched-up break for ghost snares (owned)
Modern layered clap/snare packs (Vengeance-style, Crucast-adjacent) (get elsewhere)
references: DJ Q feat. MC Bonez — You Wot! (2008)
H "Two" O feat. Platnum — What's It Gonna Be (2008)
